author: ohtadmin
title: Russian pianist at St. Matthew's Sunday
text:
A Russian pianist whose music has been dubbed “a little short of heroic” by The New York Times will perform at 2 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 16, at St. Matthew’s Episcopal Church, 87 Narragansett Ave.
The free recital by Ilya Yakushev, which is being sponsored by the Jamestown Community Piano Association, will include compositions by Mozart, Haydn, Scriabin and Rachmaninoff with music from Modest Mussorgsky’s “Pictures at an Exhibition.”
Yakushev received his first prize when he was 12 by winning a concerto competition in his native St. Petersburg. That city’s mayor then gave him the young talents award in 1997 followed by consecutive first-prize finishes (1997-98) at the Donostia Hiria International Piano Competition in San Sebastian, Spain.
After the British label Nimbus Records released Yakushev’s CD, “Prokofiev Sonatas,” the American Record Guide wrote, “Yakushev is one of the very best young pianists before the public today, and it doesn’t seem to matter what repertoire he plays. It is all of the highest caliber.”
Yakushev, during the 2024-25 season, performed more than 40 recitals in North America and Europe while appearing as a soloist for the Youngstown Symphony, Cheyenne Symphony, Panama City Symphony, St. Petersburg Philharmonic and Glacier Symphony. Highlights of his 2025-26 season include return appearances with the Pensacola Symphony, Wisconsin Chamber Orchestra and San Luis Obispo Symphony.
“Mr. Yakushev can just do about anything he wants,” The New York Times wrote in a review.
Yakushev attended the Rimsky Korsakov College of Music in St. Petersburg and subsequently came to New York City to attend Mannes College of Music, where he studied under Vladimir Feltsman.
The piano, a 7-foot Schimmel grand, was purchased by public subscription in 2001. The nonprofit organization that administers the program accepts donations to hire performers and maintain the instrument.
